While large language models struggle with producing structured output while maintaining accuracy in zero-shot information extraction tasks such as named entity recognition (NER) and relation extraction (RE), CROSSAGENTIE proposes a multi-agent framework that enhances zero-shot IE through multi-agent LLM collaboration.\n\n## Technical Approach\n\nCROSSAGENTIE refines LLM predictions iteratively through two mechanisms: intra-group cross-type debate, which resolves entity-label conflicts through context-based evidence and confidence aggregation, and inter-group cross-task debate, where NER and RE mutually refine outputs via bidirectional feedback. Additionally, the work introduces template fine-tuning, distilling high-confidence multi-agent outputs into a single model, significantly reducing inference cost while preserving accuracy.\n\n## Results\n\nExperiments across five NER and five RE datasets show that CROSSAGENTIE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art zero-shot baselines by a large margin.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8b5e6548-509b-48fe-83cf-aac2e8b9bbd1","uuid":"eb425e76-8f30-4f08-bf69-ae9ed5fac45e","timestamp":"2026-05-15T03:12:30.201Z","tool_use_result":{"query":"CROSSAGENTIE cross-agent information extraction ACL 2025","results":[{"tool_use_id":"srvtoolu_018DCXsh6JjK15hxYpPWgFVZ","content":[{"title":"CROSSAGENTIE: Cross-Type and Cross-Task Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration for Zero-Shot Information Extraction - {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01N8cG1yQivSVJ99BV5Dagix","type":"tool_result","content":"# CROSSAGENTIE Paper Information\n\n## Authors\nMeng Lu, Yuzhang Xie, Zhenyu Bi, Shuxiang Cao, and Xuan Wang\n\n## Publication Details\n- **Venue:** Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025\n- **Location:** Vienna, Austria\n- **Month/Year:** July 2025\n- **Pages:** 13953–13977\n- **DOI:** 10.18653/v1/2025.findings-acl.718\n\n## Abstract Summary\nThe paper addresses a key limitation where \"LLMs excel in generating unstructured text. However, they struggle with producing structured output while maintaining accuracy in zero-shot information extraction.\" The framework uses multi-agent collaboration through two debate mechanisms: intra-group cross-type debate for entity-label conflict resolution, and inter-group cross-task debate where NER and RE tasks provide mutual refinement. The authors also introduce template fine-tuning to distill results into a single model, reducing inference costs while maintaining accuracy.\n\n## Methodology Highlights\n- Multi-agent LLM collaboration framework\n- Iterative prediction refinement through context-based evidence and confidence aggregation\n- Bidirectional feedback between NER (named entity recognition) and RE (relation extraction) tasks\n- Template fine-tuning for efficiency\n\n## Available Links\n- **PDF:** https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.718.pdf\n- **ACL Anthology:** https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.718/\n\n*Note: No arXiv or supplementary materials links are visible on this page.*"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8b5e6548-509b-48fe-83cf-aac2e8b9bbd1","uuid":"d3faa176-a1c9-4f28-9334-13043b121a75","timestamp":"2026-05-15T03:12:58.751Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":40507,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# CROSSAGENTIE Paper Information\n\n## Authors\nMeng Lu, Yuzhang Xie, Zhenyu Bi, Shuxiang Cao, and Xuan Wang\n\n## Publication Details\n- **Venue:** Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025\n- **Location:** Vienna, Austria\n- **Month/Year:** July 2025\n- **Pages:** 13953–13977\n- **DOI:** 10.18653/v1/2025.findings-acl.718\n\n## Abstract Summary\nThe paper addresses a key limitation where \"LLMs excel in generating unstructured text. It addresses challenges with LLMs struggling to produce structured output while maintaining accuracy in zero-shot information extraction (IE), such as named entity recognition (NER) and relation extraction (RE).\n\n## Key Mechanisms\n\nCROSSAGENTIE refines LLM predictions iteratively through two mechanisms: intra-group cross-type debate, which resolves entity-label conflicts through context-based evidence and confidence aggregation, and inter-group cross-task debate, where NER and RE mutually refine outputs via bidirectional feedback.\n\n## Template Fine-Tuning\n\nThe framework introduces template fine-tuning, distilling high-confidence multi-agent outputs into a single model, significantly reducing inference cost while preserving accuracy.\n\n## Performance Results\n\nExperiments across five NER and five RE datasets show that CROSSAGENTIE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art zero-shot baselines by a large margin.\n\n## Publication\n\nCROSSAGENTIE was presented in Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8b5e6548-509b-48fe-83cf-aac2e8b9bbd1","uuid":"c75bdd7e-48e9-47e9-94dc-753368f78cac","timestamp":"2026-05-15T03:13:02.960Z","tool_use_result":{"query":"CrossAgentIE arxiv cross-type debate entity extraction zero-shot NER multi-agent","results":[{"tool_use_id":"srvtoolu_01RGCoJyHHZTf5bT2mMshkE2","content":[{"title":"CROSSAGENTIE: Cross-Type and Cross-Task Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration for Zero-Shot Information Extraction | OpenReview","url":"https://openreview.net/forum?id=OaSBRV0xMG"},{"title":"CROSSAGENTIE: Cross-Type and Cross-Task Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration for Zero-Shot Information Extraction -
